page.text:
The algebraic operation of addition induces the canonical linear order on
$\mathbb{N}$. We define $n \le m$ if and only if $m$ can be reached from
$n$ by adding some non-negative increment:
$$n \le m \iff \exists k \in \mathbb{N}, \, n + k = m$$ This relation
$\le$ is reflexive, antisymmetric, and transitive, endowing $\mathbb{N}$
with the structure of a totally ordered cancellative commutative
semiring.
